headline: Red Sox look to rebound as Giants visit Fenway Park tonight
morning_brew: It has been a rough twenty-four hours in the Hub, and I am still trying to scrub the memory of that extra-inning loss out of my brain. Giving away a game like that at Fenway Park is a tough pill to swallow, and you can bet the boys are feeling it just as much as we are. We have to flush that one down the drain immediately, because dwelling on what could have been is a quick way to let a season spiral. The schedule does not care about our feelings, and we have a fresh three-game set starting tonight against the Giants.

Looking at the standings, we are sitting at 68-59 and there is zero room for error if we want to stay in this wild card hunt. I have seen this team fight back from worse, but the consistency has to show up starting with first pitch tonight. We need to stop the bleeding and get back to playing the kind of baseball that had us feeling like a contender just a few days ago. Fenway needs to be loud tonight, because nothing wakes up a clubhouse quite like a packed yard ready to turn the page.

Elsewhere, the Patriots are grinding through camp with all the buzz around the Drake Maye and A.J. Brown connection growing by the day. It is just preseason, and I know better than to get my hopes up too early, but it is at least giving us something to talk about while the baseball team finds its footing. My old man always said that August is the longest month for a Boston sports fan, but at least we have the games to keep us honest.

news_digest.headline: Red Sox host the Giants to start 3-game series
news_digest.dans_take: A series at Fenway is exactly what we need to get back on track and wash the taste of that last heartbreaker out of our mouths.

news_digest.headline: Drake Maye-A.J. Brown connection growing at Patriots camp
news_digest.dans_take: If this connection is for real, it might actually make watching this team in the fall worth the price of a cold beer at the stadium.
